original_test_intent: Install the approved CUDA Toolkit 12 release on a confirmed native Ubuntu 22.04 arm64-SBSA DUT, preserve driver compatibility, and demonstrate toolkit/compiler plus agreed NVIDIA GPU feature parity.
original_method: Verify OS/kernel/aarch and GPU/driver support; select signed exact Toolkit release/package/hash and install mode excluding or explicitly governing bundled driver; inventory packages, libraries, environment and applications; stage rollback and drain jobs; install under approval; verify nvcc/toolkit metadata and nvidia-smi separately; run defined parity workload/feature matrix; compare logs/app health; restore only by approved package removal/environment rollback.
manual_activity: CUDA owner selects exact toolkit and parity contract and approves system changes/rollback; operator drains workloads; agent may install verified components and run defined checks.
required_inputs: Confirmed uname/OS Ubuntu 22.04 arm64-SBSA and GPU/driver matrix
Installer component policy including whether driver is excluded
Feature-parity test matrix with expected results
safety_requirements: Never execute placeholder or arbitrary latest installer
Do not infer toolkit version from nvidia-smi
Prevent unintended driver replacement or shared library overwrite
Drain GPU jobs and preserve package/environment baseline
Stop on architecture/signature/dependency/driver mismatch; no automatic reinstall
agent_execution_scope: Capture baseline and perform approved toolkit installation
engineer_actions: Resolve version/check/parity conflicts and approve components/rollback
Authorize system changes and own recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `nvcc --version` is necessary but insufficient for feature parity; credentialed SSH is unsafe, and nvidia-smi cannot prove installed toolkit version.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Install only the signed approved SBSA toolkit components, record package/library changes, verify nvcc and toolkit metadata, separately record nvidia-smi driver state, then run the approved parity matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CUDA Toolkit 12, arm64-SBSA, Ubuntu 22.04 and 30-minute estimates are retained; exact version and installer are unresolved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a reversible install manifest that separates toolkit from driver, then bind compiler/runtime metadata and each parity feature result to the exact package hash.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates placeholders and validates actual toolkit behavior rather than a driver display alone.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Driver version and CUDA compatibility value in nvidia-smi do not establish installed toolkit or feature parity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Runfile library/environment changes can break existing CUDA applications even when installation exits successfully.

project_override_considerations: CUDA owner defines exact Toolkit 12 release, component set and the feature-parity baseline for this SBSA GPU platform.
expected_evidence: Pre/post package/library/linker/environment manifest and install log
nvcc version, toolkit metadata and full nvidia-smi
Defined parity test inputs/output/exit for each feature
dmesg/XID/BMC/SEL/application health, rollback readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure mixes latest with a 12.3.1 placeholder URL/file, checks toolkit through nvidia-smi, while title requires feature parity and Criteria only mentions driver version.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution awaits an exact package and parity decision.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row284 Wistron-NV GPU-00277-V002: choose exact CUDA Toolkit 12 SBSA version instead of latest/12.3.1 placeholders; approve signed package/hash and component/driver policy, define feature-parity tests/expected results, separate nvcc/toolkit metadata from nvidia-smi driver evidence, and provide package/library/environment rollback.

review_improvement: Separates toolkit from driver, replaces placeholders with immutable artifacts and turns feature parity into explicit executable coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: nvidia-smi reports the loaded driver and a maximum compatible CUDA API, not which toolkit is installed. A runfile can also install or overwrite driver/user libraries unless components are constrained. Native SBSA packages and x86 packages are not interchangeable, and feature parity requires defined compile/runtime behaviors beyond version strings.
